opportunities.title: User service should not store or expose credential fields
opportunities.summary: ## Bug Current `apps/api/src/services/userService.js` stores the entire caller-controlled payload and returns stored user objects directly: ```js const user = { id: `usr_${Date.now()}`, ...payload }; users.push(user); return user; ``` `listUsers()` then returns the same objects unchanged. If a caller supplies credential/private fields such as `password`, `passwordHash`, `token`, or `resetToken`, those values are persisted in the in-memory user list, echoed by the create response, and exposed again by the user-list response. ## Expected behavior - User records should store only intended public/profile fields. - Credential/private fields such as `password`, `passwordHash`, `token`, and `resetToken` must not appear in create-user responses or `listUsers()` output. - Preserve legitimate public user fields and server-owned IDs. - Add focused regression coverage for both create and list behavior. ## Scope Keep production changes focused on `apps/api/src/services/userService.js` plus focused service regression tests. opportunities.title: RFC: named review budget per pool (second cash line for reviewers)
opportunities.summary: # RFC: a named review budget per pool, so review pay never dilutes the author pool **Amended 2026-09-01** to adopt the additive-only invariant, following [mashingaan's analysis](https://github.com/SlopDotCash/slopdotcash/issues/303#issuecomment-5500417981) of live leaderboard data. The original draft allocated review events from the review line instead of the shared pool; that split could have paid reviewers less than they receive today. The amended design keeps the shared pool byte for byte unchanged and makes the review line strictly additive. **TL;DR:** Projects that fund a monthly contributor pool should be able to commit a second, smaller cash line that pays reviewers. Today, review points share the single monthly pool with authored work, so every hour of review a contributor does makes the authors' slices smaller. This proposal adds an optional `reviewBudget` block to the project manifest, pays reviewers from that line at cycle close **on top of the unchanged shared pool**, and shows it as its own line on the pool card and in the allocation table. opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
